name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Fade H1's extremes: hold the AI-disruption-fear and macro-beaten-down names with real turnaround catalysts (ADBE/CRM, oversold crypto, small caps, gold), sized down on the one leg facing an imminent binary event and up on the legs where this week's news confirmed the thesis.
reassessment_note: Kept the same six-name turnaround book and the same 58% gross / 42% cash structure, but resized within it based on what actually happened this week rather than doing a full rebuild. Biggest change: ADBE reports Q3 earnings on 2026-09-10, two trading days after this leg would re-enter, and sell-side has split hard into the print -- RBC just raised its target to $315 (Buy) while Morgan Stanley cut ADBE to Underweight at $240 on the view that AI substitution is structurally eating Creative Cloud's recurring revenue. That is a real binary event risk sitting right on top of a leg that is already the book's worst performer (-8.98%), so I cut it from 17% to 10% rather than holding full size or exiting the turnaround thesis outright. I funded that trim plus a partial cash redeployment by adding to the legs where the tape confirmed rather than complicated the thesis: CRM (Agentforce-driven re-rating still running, TD Cowen just lifted its target to $300 and the stock has round-tripped from a $144 YTD low to $259), BTC/ETH (Bitcoin holding above $81k on the largest ETF inflows in nine months, Ethereum's August was its strongest month of 2026 and it's still above the $2,438 level bulls need for a continued push), and IWM (small-cap uptrend intact with sell-side eyeing $300-330, a broadening-beyond-financials read on the same NIM/rate-relief story that's driving KRE elsewhere). I trimmed GLD from 10% to 8%, not because the long-term case is broken (JPMorgan still sees $6,000/oz by year-end) but because the August jobs report (162k vs. 55k expected, released just before this cutoff) pushed Sept FOMC rate-hike odds to roughly 58% as of the 9/4 close -- a genuine near-term headwind for a non-yielding asset that argues for a smaller hedge, not a larger one, right now.

positions.thesis: Cut from 17% to 10% ahead of the 2026-09-10 Q3 print. The turnaround thesis (AI-disruption fear on Creative Cloud is overdone) is intact and RBC just raised its target to $315, but Morgan Stanley's fresh Underweight/$240 call on AI-substitution risk means the print is now a genuine coin-flip catalyst on the book's worst leg (-8.98%); sizing down lets the thesis stay in the book through the event without a full-size bet on a binary outcome.

Increased from 8% to 12%. The Agentforce-driven turnaround is confirmed and still running -- TD Cowen just raised its target to $300 (Buy reiterated), the stock has round-tripped from a $144 YTD low to $259, and FQ2 revenue of $11.35B drove a 12% surge on the print. This is the working half of the AI-fear-fade pair; press it while ADBE's print risk argues for caution on the other half.

Increased from 8% to 10%. BTC is holding above $81k on the largest ETF inflow in nine months after Fed Governor Waller's rate-steady comments; still a turnaround/oversold-crypto position from the H1 fear washout, and the flow data this week confirms rather than challenges that thesis.

Increased from 7% to 8%. August was ETH's strongest month of 2026 (+32.5%), spot-ETF inflows are supporting the recovery, and ETH remains above the $2,438 level bulls need to keep the $2,920 upside case alive -- kept as the smaller half of the crypto sleeve given repeated rejection near $2,550 shows the move isn't fully confirmed yet.

Increased from 8% to 10%. Small-cap uptrend intact with sell-side targets in the $300-330 range on Q2 earnings showing the first full quarter of rate-relief benefit; this is the same NIM/rate-easing tailwind lifting KRE-type financials broadening into the Russell 2000, and it is the turnaround book's cleanest confirmed-momentum leg this week. No take-profit, consistent with running this as a trend position rather than a bounce trade.

Trimmed from 10% to 8%. Long-term case is intact (JPMorgan still targets $6,000/oz by year-end and gold is already ~22% off its January record, i.e. the oversold/turnaround entry logic still applies), but the hot August jobs report pushed Sept FOMC rate-hike odds to roughly 58% as of the 9/4 close, a real near-term headwind for a non-yielding hedge -- smaller position, same direction.
